text:
maya: Hey team, customer on dedicated-eu-2 is seeing intermittent 502s and a kernel oops on the node running their tenant. Sample request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d4e. Happened ~2025-08-11T16:12:xxZ and again ~16:18:xxZ. Need repro/log capture instructions so we can hand this to infra.

ivan: Can you paste the earliest request-id and a minimal curl repro? Also which pod and node? We'll need both pod logs and node dmesg/journalctl + GPU metrics.

maya: earliest: rq_0a1b2c3d4e, later: rq_0f9e8d7c6b. Pod: inference-serve-7-5c9b8 (container runtime). Node: gke-dedicated-eu-2-node-13. Customer says it happened while sending a ~1k token prompt.

lia: OK. Steps to collect (quick checklist):
- reproduce with curl to capture the exact request-id header
- kubectl logs + kubectl describe for the pod
- on node: journalctl -k, dmesg, /var/log/syslog around the timestamp
- GPU: nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY + nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,memory.total,memory.used --format=csv -l 1 (10s)
- capture /proc/driver/nvidia/version and driver dmesg

ivan: Example curl (use their API key):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \ 
  -H "x-request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d4e-repro" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood/large-v1","input":"hello"}'
```
Add `-v` so we capture headers and timings. If the customer is routing through a proxy, use `--resolve` to target the cluster VIP.

maya: Running the curl now, will paste the verbose output.

support-bot: Reminder: use the debug helper `redwood-debug collect --request-id rq_0a1b2c3d4e` if available on the node; it bundles pod logs, kube describe, and common node artifacts. Upload target: s3://redwood-support-bundles/1757770000/ (expiry 7 days).

maya: verbose curl shows a TCP connection established, then HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway. Response contains: `\{"error":"upstream reset"\}`.

ivan: On the pod, run: `kubectl -n tenant-42 logs inference-serve-7-5c9b8 -c runtime --since=30m > pod_runtime.log` and `kubectl -n tenant-42 describe pod inference-serve-7-5c9b8 > pod_describe.txt`.

ivan: On the node (ssh required), collect:
```
# dmesg around timestamp
sudo journalctl -k --since "2025-08-11 16:00:00" --until "2025-08-11 16:30:00" > node_kernel.log
# kernel ring buffer snapshot
sudo dmesg -T | sed -n '1,200p' > dmesg_snapshot.txt
# GPU state
sudo nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY > nvidia_memory.txt
sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,memory.total,memory.used --format=csv -l 1 -f nvidia_timeseries.csv &
# run that for ~10s then kill the background pid
```

lia: Also capture driver info: `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version` and `sudo dmesg | grep -i nvrm -n > nvrm-dmesg.txt`. If there's an oops, include the full oops block.

maya: I grabbed a short kernel oops snippet from journalctl: 
```
[  123.456789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, GPU has fallen off the bus. HINT: Try the latest driver.
[  123.456792] kernel: BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0000000000000000
[  123.456795] kernel: RIP: 0010:some_module+0xabc/0x1000
```

ivan: Good, that looks like an NVRM/Xid event. Please keep the node alive (no reboot) and tar the collected logs: `tar czf 1757770000-debug-bundle.tgz pod_runtime.log pod_describe.txt node_kernel.log dmesg_snapshot.txt nvidia_memory.txt nvidia_timeseries.csv nvrm-dmesg.txt proc_nvidia_version.txt`.

ops-bot: Heads-up: copying /var/log may require elevated access. Confirm you have ops approval before transferring large node files off-prem. :lock:

maya: I have ops approval. Uploading bundle to s3 now.

support-bot: Upload complete: s3://redwood-support-bundles/1757770000/1757770000-debug-bundle.tgz (size 18.3 MB).

lia: Thanks. Next steps: 1) we'll correlate timestamps with GPU metrics to see memory pressure spikes; 2) pass the bundle to the driver team for Xid analysis; 3) recommend temporary mitigation: pin the tenant to a different node pool or reduce batch size/sequence length.

ivan: Also add the application-level trace: `curl -H "x-request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d4e"` and include `runtime.trace_id` if your SDK emits it. That helps map tokens -> kernel activity.

maya: Noted. I'll include the curl trace + spans in the ticket. Thanks all :thumbsup:

lia: We'll create a follow-up incident PR and link this bundle. If driver confirms a hardware/driver issue we'll schedule evac for that node.

maya: marking this thread resolved for now — will reopen if we see more occurrences.
